title: Dissent by kind of file
question: Which kinds of money file draw a no vote most often?
finding: Appropriation and budget ordinances draw a no most often: 42 of 257 (16.3%), against 82 of 3,226 (2.5%) for every other kind together. The largest group, contract or other agreement, has 38 of 1,089 (3.5%). Grant or gift the City accepts: 17 of 900 (1.9%). Lease, licence or concession: 13 of 625 (2.1%). Grant agreement: 6 of 203 (3.0%). Emergency declaration or contract: 3 of 56 (5.4%). Property purchase or sale: 3 of 54 (5.6%). Settlement with a business: 1 of 197 (0.5%). Loan: 1 of 102 (1.0%). All 3,483 files together name $66.59 billion in their titles.
how: Each file is put in one kind by the words of its title, the first match winning in this order: appropriation or budget ordinance; settlement with a business; grant or gift the City accepts (“accept and expend”); loan; lease, licence or concession; grant agreement; property purchase or sale; emergency declaration or contract; any other contract or agreement. Dollars are the total each title names; for an appropriation ordinance an amount is taken only where the title plainly states one total (102 of 257), and the annual budget ordinances are left without one. “Part of a same-day list” counts files whose no came with 2 or more other money files on the same day and the same line-up of votes.
limits: A unanimous vote is the ordinary result and no sign of anything wrong. 3,419 of the 3,483 files were recommended by a committee before the Board voted, 900 accept a grant or gift, and 1,104 amend or extend an agreement already in place. Of the 770 files of $10 million or more introduced since 2019, 650 carry a report by the Board’s Budget and Legislative Analyst among their attachments, so a vote with no dissent can follow written scrutiny at the committee stage. A no vote is ordinary; the vote pages give no reasons, and dissent can reflect a disagreement about policy or the budget rather than doubt about the organization named in the file. Dollar figures are the totals named in file titles: an agreement amended twice is counted at each new total, rent and accepted grants are money coming to the City as well as money going out, and budget ordinances name no single figure, so a sum of title dollars measures what the titles name, not money spent. Settlements with individuals and tax-refund settlements are not among these files. For 332 roll calls the Clerk’s vote page says “by the following vote” and lists no member, 306 of them dated 2016-04-13 to 2016-07-26; 315 were read instead from the vote lines in the Clerk’s published minutes of the same meeting, and 17 remain without member votes and are counted nowhere here. 1 money file (160358) whose final passage is among them is left out of the counts, and none is counted as unanimous. 104 of the final votes counted here were read from the minutes. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
